bipartite.kami_theme: Comparing present feelings after having met and consummated the relationship with the beloved, using the standard 'kurabureba' comparison structure to measure emotional states across time
bipartite.shimo_theme: Realization that former longing before the meeting was, by comparison, not real suffering at all — the present post-union yearning is far more intense
bipartite.pivot_note: The kami-no-ku sets up an act of comparison (くらぶれば, 'when I compare') between the emotional state now, after having met/been intimate, against the past. The pivot at くらぶれば turns the poem: rather than resolving into contentment after union, the shimo-no-ku delivers the paradoxical realization that the anguish of longing has only deepened after the meeting — the past unfulfilled longing (which felt like suffering at the time) now seems by contrast to have been no suffering ('物を思はざりけり') at all. This is the classic paradox of post-union love poetry: consummation intensifies rather than resolves desire.

kigo.note: This poem is a love poem (koi-uta) without any seasonal image; 逢ひ見て refers to a romantic meeting/consummation and carries no seasonal connotation. No flowers, birds, moon, dew, frost, or other conventional seasonal markers appear anywhere in the text — the poem belongs to the koi (love) category of the anthology rather than a seasonal category.

source_jp:
逢ひ見ての
後の心に
くらぶれば
むかしは物を
思はざりけり
